intro: An optimizer update and its learning-rate schedule solve different problems. Specify the boundary steps so warmup and decay join without a jump.
task: Implement a linear warmup followed by cosine decay. Check the exact warmup boundary, midpoint, and final step rather than relying on a plot.
requirements: step, total_steps and warmup_steps are integers, excluding booleans. Require step>=0, total_steps>0, and 0<=warmup_steps<total_steps.
Require finite real rates with 0<=min_lr<=max_lr. During step<warmup_steps, return max_lr*step/warmup_steps.
For warmup_steps<=step<total_steps use progress=(step-warmup_steps)/(total_steps-warmup_steps) and min_lr+0.5*(max_lr-min_lr)*(1+cos(pi*progress)). At or after total_steps return min_lr.
Return a numeric scalar. With no warmup, step zero starts at max_lr; with warmup, step zero starts at zero, even when min_lr is positive.
Inputs must be real numeric values with finite magnitude at most 1e30. Leave inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Handle intervals in order
hints.body: Deal with warmup and completed schedules before calculating the cosine progress.

hints.title: Check the midpoint
hints.body: Halfway through the decay interval, the rate is the arithmetic mean of the peak and minimum.

explanation: Warmup controls the initial ramp independently of the decay floor. The minimum rate is the floor for the decay phase, not for warmup.
The peak occurs exactly at warmup_steps. At total_steps the cosine reaches its minimum, and clamping subsequent steps avoids an unintended second rise.
The schedule is adapted from the upstream scalar function. Added validation rules remove ambiguous configurations such as a warmup that occupies the entire schedule.
